points: The Nov 2 Q3 print will show whether the Q2 momentum — reports suggest a consensus beat and guidance raise — carried through the summer, a key test with the 90-day revenue estimate up 11.21% and 15 upward analyst revisions versus zero down in the last 30 days.
It will reveal if restaurant-level margins and cost controls held in Q3, supporting the ~19.7% FY1 EPS growth consensus and the long case that earnings momentum is intact.
Management's updated full-year guidance will show whether the expected FY2 slowdown to ~9.9% EPS growth is stable or whether Q4 needs to be cut; a steady or raised outlook supports the long.
Peer prints from BJRI, BROS, SHAK and EAT clustered from Oct 28 to Nov 19 will provide read-throughs on casual-dining demand, pricing power and labor/commodity pressure around CAKE's report.

The valuation flag is fair — P/E at 0.9x the theme median and PEG at 0.7x the theme median — so the long relies on the print proving the growth trajectory is not already priced in relative to restaurants.
Q3 commentary on off-premise, catering and new-unit progress will shape the Q4 holiday setup and whether the FY2 consensus EPS of $4.96 is achievable.
watch: 30-day analyst revision ratio stays lopsidedly positive (15 up / 0 down or better) — supports the long.
FY1 EPS growth stays near 19.7% and FY2 growth does not fall materially below FY1 — supports the long.
PEG1 stays at or below ~1.24, near 0.7x the theme median — supports the long.
90-day revenue estimate change stays positive — supports the long.
